title: Best Pet Cameras UK
short: Wi-Fi and 4G pet cameras compared for picture quality, ease of setup and real-world reliability, from treat-dispensing favourites to subscription-free outdoor options.
intro: A pet camera's real test is whether it's still earning its keep months after the novelty wears off. This guide compares cameras tested by the PetsRadar team for more than six months each, with named testers assessing picture quality, setup, and whether each model was genuinely worth the money.

products.name: 360° View Camera
products.best_for: Buyers who want a treat-dispensing camera with pet-specific alerts
products.key_spec: 1080p, 360° view, treat dispenser (up to 100 treats), barking alerts, no subscription required for core features
products.summary: PetsRadar's top pick, holding up to 100 treats you can dispense remotely for an interactive experience even when you're not home. Tester Barbara found it very easy to set up and user-friendly, with the 360° feature tracking and recording your pet so you don't miss a moment, though picture quality isn't perfect and advanced features like the AI health checker need a subscription.

specs.Subscription: Not required for core features ($5.38/month for extras)

cons: Picture quality isn't the best in the group

products.name: Go PT Ultra Plus
products.best_for: Buyers who want an outdoor camera with no Wi-Fi or subscription needed
products.key_spec: 4K resolution, 355° pan/140° tilt, 4G LTE connectivity, colour night vision, no subscription
products.summary: PetsRadar's editor Georgia tested this on the side of her pony's stable for months and says she now 'can't live without it', screwing it to a roof and finding it quick and easy to set up. It doesn't need Wi-Fi, running instead on a 4G SIM card, with impressive 4K resolution and colour night vision, though the trade-off is needing a 4G network to function.
cons: Requires a 4G network and SIM card
products.search: Reolink Go PT Ultra Plus camera

products.name: ROLA PetPal
products.best_for: Buyers who want a camera that doubles as an interactive toy
products.key_spec: 2.5K resolution, 135° field of view, built-in laser and treat dispenser, drives over 15mm obstacles
products.summary: PetsRadar's Megan Milstead tested this robot camera-toy hybrid herself, finding it simple to set up with hours of fun watching cats investigate it up close. It can be driven around the house via app with a built-in laser, treat dispenser and pre-recorded sounds, though the battery life isn't the best and picture/audio quality trail rivals.
pros: Doubles as an interactive toy with laser and treat dispenser
cons: Not the best audio or picture quality

products.name: 4K Spotlight Indoor/Outdoor
products.best_for: Buyers who want a genuine security camera that also watches pets
products.key_spec: 4K resolution, colour night vision, person/vehicle/animal detection, weatherproof to -4°F to 131°F
products.summary: PetsRadar's tester Thomas found the app very simple, breaking up recordings by calendar day with relatively good picture quality that clearly identified faces from a distance. It doesn't need a subscription, includes a 32GB MicroSD card, and can detect people, animals, packages and vehicles, though you'll need multiple units to cover a wide area.
pros: Weatherproof for indoor or outdoor use
cons: Needs multiple cameras to cover a wide area

products.name: Wireless Security Camera S4
products.best_for: Buyers who want a cable-free camera that's easy to reposition
products.key_spec: 2K QHD resolution, 140° field of view, customisable trigger zones, weatherproof
products.summary: PetsRadar's tester Dan found the 2K picture 'very good' during the day and great for facial recognition, praising how simple the wireless design was to install anywhere. When placed outside in the rain, the speaker sounded quiet and muffled, but Toucan swiftly sent a replacement that worked perfectly, and the battery lasted around a week per charge.
pros: Fully wireless, easy to position anywhere
cons: Trigger zone setting isn't precise enough
Audio quality dropped in wet weather on the tester's original unit

products.name: Indoor Camera
products.best_for: Buyers who want the option to physically block the camera when not in use
products.key_spec: 1080p HD, manual privacy cover, colour night vision, Alexa compatible
products.summary: The cheapest model in PetsRadar's test, yet tester Matthew found it offers 'great full-color picture quality' and captures footage instantly. Its standout feature is a manual privacy panel you swivel over the lens and microphone without unplugging the camera, though recording and reviewing footage requires a Ring Protect subscription.
pros: Manual privacy cover for the lens and microphone
Great full-colour picture quality for the price
cons: Subscription needed to record and review footage

products.name: Mini 2
products.best_for: Buyers who want solid basics at a low price
products.key_spec: 1080p HD, weather-resistant, two-way talk, motion detection
products.summary: PetsRadar's tester Lindsey found this budget camera super easy to set up, taking about five minutes, with picture quality she called pretty good and clear for a small screen. It's weather-resistant for indoor or outdoor placement, though it lacks any pet-specific detection or interactive features like treat tossing.
pros: Good picture quality for the price
Night vision and motion detection included
cons: No pet-specific detection or treat dispensing
Fewer interactive features than dedicated pet cameras

products.name: Seek Pan & Tilt Camera
products.best_for: Buyers who want to adjust the camera's view without moving it physically
products.key_spec: 1080p HD, AI human detection, remote pan and tilt, pre-recorded broadcasts
products.summary: PetsRadar's tester Chloe found the picture quality good enough for the camera's intended use, if not amazing, and particularly liked being able to adjust the camera's position remotely from the app. It adds AI-powered human detection and two-way communication alongside the pan and tilt function.
pros: Remote pan and tilt from the app
cons: Picture quality is adequate rather than excellent

guide.q: Do I need a camera with a subscription?
guide.a: Not necessarily. Models like the Reolink Go PT Ultra Plus and Lorex 4K Spotlight here work fully without a monthly fee, while others like the Furbo and Ring here offer core features for free but lock extras like extended footage history or the AI health checker behind a subscription. Decide whether you need those extra features before paying for an ongoing plan.

guide.q: Do pet cameras record all the time?
guide.a: Most pet cameras only record when triggered by motion or sound, which helps with spotting behaviour patterns and saves on storage space. A handful of models offer continuous recording that overwrites older footage after a set period, like a week, which is worth seeking out if you want an unbroken record rather than triggered clips.

guide.q: Can a pet camera help with separation anxiety?
guide.a: Vet Dr Rebecca MacMillan says cameras are a 'useful aid' for monitoring a pet's behaviour and progress with training, letting owners spot signs of anxiety like pacing or excessive panting. A camera with two-way audio, like the Furbo or Enabot here, can also let you talk to a distressed pet remotely, though it isn't a direct cure on its own.

guide.q: Wi-Fi or 4G: which connection type should I choose?
guide.a: A standard Wi-Fi camera, like the Ring Indoor or Blink Mini 2 here, is simpler and cheaper to run but needs a strong home Wi-Fi signal to work reliably. A 4G camera like the Reolink Go PT Ultra Plus here is better suited to outbuildings, stables or gardens beyond Wi-Fi range, at the cost of needing a SIM card and data plan.
